correctness.rationale: For every cutting hyperplane, one cut piece contains a central half-cube after orienting the offset. Cube symmetries reduce the central normal to ordered nonnegative coordinates. Two exhaustive inequalities on those coordinates produce explicit point pairs in the half-cube whose squared distance is at least nine. The coordinate central cut attains diameter three in the scaled cube, hence three halves in the unit cube.

value.rationale: The unit three-cube with one hyperplane cut is a canonical exact instance of the diameter min-max division problem. The result closes the gap between the primary source’s general lower bound and its coordinate-mesh upper bound in this first spatial cube case, using an orientation-uniform geometric witness rather than a numerical search or arbitrary parameter slice.
